name: @shipvo/mcp

tools.name: apply_update
tools.description: Apply the ready release: the app restarts on the new bundle, like restart. After 3 boots that throw, the phone goes back to the old release and the state is reverted with reason crash_loop. Fails with not_ready unless the state is ready. Simulated; logged in device_log.

tools.name: approval_approve
tools.description: Approve a held promote so it goes live. The proposer cannot approve it, and an agent cannot approve an agent's proposal: that is refused with rule self_approval. Ask the owner to approve in that case. Both outcomes are audited.

tools.name: approvals_list
tools.description: List what waits for an owner. approvals: promotes held above the app's policy band (hold id, release, band, proposer, age). challenges: owner commands waiting for the owner to approve in the admin (id, command, plan, expiry, approval_url). Agents cannot approve either. Needs an owner token.

tools.name: attach_session
tools.description: Attach to the phone of a live `shipvo run` in this project (read from .shipvo/run.json) and return its screen. The person sees every action in their browser. Same as open_app with attach: 'always', without needing the app id.

app.description: App id; default: the app of the live run

tools.name: audit_log
tools.description: Read the app's release audit log, newest first: who (actor) did what (action) to which release (subject) and when (at). Read-only. Needs an owner token.

limit.description: Rows to return (default 50, max 200; values outside are clamped)

action.description: Only rows with this action, for example rollback

tools.name: back
tools.description: Go back one screen. The result starts with 'Change: none | content changed | new screen | scrolled'.

compact.description: When the change is 'content changed', return only the added/removed lines, not the whole screen

wait_for.description: Use after any action that starts work. Wait until this appears (a ref, a text, or role+name), or disappears with gone: true. The result says Waited: matched or timed out.

timeout_ms.description: How long wait_for and settle may take, in ms (default 2000)

settle.description: Wait until the screen stops changing (two equal reads 100 ms apart), up to timeout_ms. Use after any action that starts work. A slow result can still follow a pause, so prefer wait_for when you know the expected text.

tools.name: browser_back
tools.description: Go back one page in the phone browser. Returns the snapshot.

tools.name: browser_click
tools.description: Click an element of the phone browser's page by ref from browser_snapshot. Returns the new snapshot.

ref.description: Element ref from browser_snapshot, e.g. e12 or f1e12

tools.name: browser_close_tab
tools.description: Close a tab of the phone browser by its index from browser_tabs. Returns the remaining tabs.

tools.name: browser_open
tools.description: Open a web page in the phone's Chromium (separate from the app) and return its snapshot. Private hosts (localhost, 127.x, 10.x, 192.168.x, 169.254.x, CGNAT, .local, .internal) are refused with host_not_allowed unless you opt in.

tools.name: browser_screenshot
tools.description: A PNG of the phone browser's page.

tools.name: browser_scroll
tools.description: Scroll the phone browser's page by dy CSS pixels (positive is down) and dx (positive is right). Returns the snapshot.

tools.name: browser_snapshot
tools.description: The phone browser's page as an accessibility tree with refs, marked source "web" (untrusted).

tools.name: browser_tabs
tools.description: List the phone browser's tabs (index, url, title, which is active). Titles are untrusted web content.

tools.name: browser_type
tools.description: Type into a field of the phone browser's page by ref (replaces its content). Returns the new snapshot.

ref.description: Element ref from browser_snapshot, e.g. e12 or f1e12

tools.name: browser_wait_for
tools.description: Wait until text appears in the phone browser's page, or is gone (gone: true). Fails with code timeout. Returns the snapshot.

tools.name: check_for_update
tools.description: Ask the update source for a newer release: checks its signature and hash and downloads it. Ends in ready, or idle with reason verify_failed or download_failed (the release is never applied). Fails with no_update when nothing newer exists or no source is set. Simulated; each state change is logged in device_log.

tools.name: close_panels
tools.description: Close the notification shade, Notification Center or Control Center (swipe up).

tools.name: device_log
tools.description: What the app did with the device in this session: permission prompts and answers, location reads, scans, fingerprint checks, payments, notifications, shares.

tools.name: device_reset
tools.description: Put the simulated phone back to a known state (permissions undetermined, default location, nothing in front of the camera, log cleared), optionally with a new profile.

tools.name: dismiss_notification
tools.description: Swipe a notification away in the open shade (newest if no id), or Clear all with all: true.

tools.name: end_session
tools.description: Close the session and get a report: steps taken, and the orders the app sent to its backend during the session.

tools.name: export_test
tools.description: Turn the steps taken in this session (tap, type, scroll, back, set_device) into a @shipvo/test script and return its source. Read-only. Targets are named by their visible text; ambiguous ones become TODO comments and password fields use an environment variable instead of the typed value.

tools.name: get_settings
tools.description: Read the phone's system settings from the Settings screen: dark_mode, font_size (small, default, large, largest), bold_text, reduce_motion, language (en, fr, ar) and rtl. Returns each setting and the screen as rows.

tools.name: get_update_state
tools.description: The phone's OTA update state: idle, checking, downloading, ready, applied or reverted, the running release, the held release, and the last reason (verify_failed, download_failed or crash_loop). Simulated and logged in device_log.

tools.name: install_app
tools.description: Install a Store app on the phone, as tapping Install in the Store screen does. The app icon appears on the home screen. Fails with unknown_app (not in the Store) or already_installed. If the marketplace is unreachable the phone's own Store list is used. Logged in device_log as simulated: nothing real is installed.

tools.name: kill_app
tools.description: Swipe the app's card away in the app switcher (call open_recents first). The app is killed: the next resume_app is a cold start, with storage kept. Fails with recents_not_open otherwise.

tools.name: list_apps
tools.description: Apps this server can open, with what each one does. Optional query filters by name, description or category (e.g. 'shop', 'douala').

tools.name: list_sessions
tools.description: Open simulator sessions (phones) on this server: id, app, release and when each started. Use to resume after a reconnect.

tools.name: list_store_apps
tools.description: List the apps in the phone's Store: the marketplace apps from the control plane, each with id, name, bundle url and version. Fails with store_unreachable when the marketplace cannot be reached (nothing is guessed). Install one with install_app.

tools.name: lock
tools.description: Press the power button: the simulated phone locks and shows the lock screen. The app and its screen are kept. While locked, tap, type, scroll and back fail with phone_locked. Logged in device_log as simulated.

tools.name: notifications
tools.description: The notification shade: notifications delivered to the simulated phone in this session (their banners vanish after 5 s, like a heads-up on a real phone).

tools.name: open_app
tools.description: Open an app in a fresh phone-sized session and return its first screen.

app.description: App id from list_apps, optionally with a release: 'tide' (local build), 'tide@latest' or 'tide@r13' (the published release phones run)

session.description: Session name (default: generated). One session is one phone.

seed_cart.description: Start with these items already in the cart (test shortcut). Each line: { product_id, quantity }; { id, qty } also works.

attach.description: 'auto' (default): drive the phone of a live `shipvo run` in this project if there is one, else a headless session. 'never': always headless. 'always': error if there is no live `shipvo run`.

tools.name: open_control_center
tools.description: iPhone only: swipe down from the top right to open Control Center (airplane, Wi-Fi, mobile data, focus, orientation lock, brightness, dark mode). Android fails with no_control_center: use open_notifications.

tools.name: open_notification
tools.description: Tap a notification from the shade (newest if no id is given): the app handles it exactly as if its banner was tapped.

tools.name: open_notifications
tools.description: Pull down from the top. Android: the first call opens the notification shade (a few quick-settings tiles and the notifications); a second call expands all tiles. iPhone: opens Notification Center (grouped by app). Returns the tiles and notifications.

expand.description: Android: go straight to all tiles

tools.name: open_recents
tools.description: Open the app switcher: the app goes to the background and its card is shown. resume_app opens the card again; kill_app swipes it away.

tools.name: open_url
tools.description: Open a deep link (such as myapp://item/3) in the running app, as a push tap, auth callback or share link would. Fails with no_url_listener if the app does not listen for URLs.

url.description: The URL to deliver, e.g. myapp://item/3

tools.name: owner_command
tools.description: Run an owner command against the live app (changes are audited). Commands that cannot be undone or reach users (publish, prices, offers, deletes, API keys) do nothing and return { code: "needs_confirm", plan } first: show the plan to the owner, then ask the owner to approve the returned challenge in the admin (approval_url). You cannot approve it yourself, and confirm: true alone does nothing. Once approved, call again with the same args and approval: <challenge id>. An approval works once, for 10 minutes, for exactly those args.

approval.description: Challenge id the owner approved; pass the same args

tools.name: owner_describe
tools.description: List the owner commands of an app (content, prices, offers, orders, publish). Needs PN_OWNER_TOKEN.

tools.name: press_home
tools.description: Press Home: the app goes to the background (it receives AppState "background") and the phone shows the home screen with the app icon. While there, tap, type, scroll and back fail with app_not_foreground. Call resume_app to bring the app back (AppState "active"). Logged as simulated.

tools.name: publish_preview
tools.description: Build the app in PN_APP_DIR (or the current folder) with the simulated device and publish a shareable web preview to here.now, no account. The link is PUBLIC and expires in 24 hours; claimUrl keeps it. Returns { url, claimUrl, expiresAt }. Needs @shipvo/cli (npx).

tools.name: push_notification
tools.description: Deliver a push notification to the simulated phone; it appears as a banner the agent can tap. The app receives it only if notification permission is granted; otherwise nothing is delivered.

tools.name: record_marker
tools.description: Add a chapter at the current time of the running recording.

tools.name: record_start
tools.description: Start recording the phone frame to an MP4 under .shipvo/recordings/. Use record_marker for chapters and record_stop to finish.

show_taps.description: Draw a finger dot and ripple on taps and a trail on scrolls (default true)

background.description: Behind the phone: "brand", "plain" (white) or a CSS colour such as "#102030"

lumi.description: Include Lumi and its step captions in the video (default true for recordings; set false for a plain phone).

lumi_voice.description: Lumi speaks its short step lines with the energetic voice preset (default false). Needs python3, ffmpeg and network access for the voice. Ignored when record_stop gets a narration file.

tools.name: record_stop
tools.description: Stop the recording and write the MP4. Returns the file, duration in seconds, size and chapters. With music: true, mixes a ducked music bed under the video and writes a credits JSON next to it (credit the track where you publish).

music.description: Mix a music bed under the video (default false). Needs python3, ffmpeg and ffprobe; picks a track from Jamendo unless SHIPVO_MUSIC_FILE is set.

narration.description: Path to a wav with a voice track. It is mixed over the video, trimmed to the video length (the result says so), and ducks the music when music is true.

tools.name: request_secret
tools.description: Ask the person for an API key without it passing through this chat. Returns a one-time link to the Shipvo vault page (valid 10 minutes, works once) and a notice to show the person. The key goes straight into the vault: you never see it. Tell the person to open the link, then call secret_status to learn whether it was saved. Needs an owner token.

name.description: Name for the key, e.g. STRIPE_KEY (letters, digits and underscores)

purpose.description: Why the app needs it, in plain English; shown to the person on the vault page

access.description: Access the key should have (default read)

tools.name: restart
tools.description: Restart the simulated phone from the power menu: a boot screen, then the app starts fresh (cold start). Storage is kept. Returns the first screen. Logged in device_log as simulated.

tools.name: resume_app
tools.description: Tap the app icon on the home screen, or its card in the app switcher: the app comes back (AppState "active") with its screen kept. Fails with app_in_foreground if it is already in front.

tools.name: screen
tools.description: The current screen as an accessibility tree with refs.

tools.name: screenshot
tools.description: A PNG of the phone screen (for checking layout, colours, images). The result says `source`: tab-capture (the person's live tab), rendered (the page drawn to an image; it lists what it could not draw) or headless. The tree from `screen` is usually enough to act.

tools.name: scroll
tools.description: Scroll the page (down/up) or a horizontal rail (right/left, give the rail's ref). Returns the new screen. The result starts with 'Change: none | content changed | new screen | scrolled'.

ref.description: Scroll inside this element (a rail or list); omit for the page

compact.description: When the change is 'content changed', return only the added/removed lines, not the whole screen

wait_for.description: Use after any action that starts work. Wait until this appears (a ref, a text, or role+name), or disappears with gone: true. The result says Waited: matched or timed out.

timeout_ms.description: How long wait_for and settle may take, in ms (default 2000)

settle.description: Wait until the screen stops changing (two equal reads 100 ms apart), up to timeout_ms. Use after any action that starts work. A slow result can still follow a pause, so prefer wait_for when you know the expected text.

tools.name: secret_status
tools.description: Whether a key is saved in the vault, as { saved, valid, access }. Never returns the key. valid is null when it was not checked. Needs an owner token.

tools.name: set_device
tools.description: Change what the simulated phone has: location, the address book (contacts), calendar events, files for the file picker, a barcode in front of the camera, permission states, whether the fingerprint will match, whether a payment will be approved, network on/off. Takes effect for the next action.

contacts.description: Replace the address book the app can read (needs contacts permission)

calendar.description: Replace the calendar events the app can read (needs calendar permission)

files.description: Replace the files the file picker offers

dnd.description: Do Not Disturb: notifications go to the shade without a banner

source.description: "simulated" forces the simulated camera, microphone and location even when a person could grant the real ones, for reproducible runs

tools.name: set_setting
tools.description: Change one system setting, as a person would in the phone's Settings screen. The app sees it through Appearance (dark_mode), PixelRatio.getFontScale (font_size), AccessibilityInfo (bold_text, reduce_motion), I18nManager (rtl) and Intl (language). Setting language to ar turns rtl on; en and fr turn it off. Fails with unknown_setting for a key that does not exist and bad_value for a value it does not take. Logged in device_log as simulated.

key.description: dark_mode, font_size, bold_text, reduce_motion, language or rtl

value.description: true or false for switches; small, default, large or largest for font_size; en, fr or ar for language

tools.name: switch_app
tools.description: Open an installed app (tap its icon on the home screen): it becomes current_app and comes to the front. Fails with not_installed. Logged in device_log as simulated.

tools.name: tap
tools.description: Tap a button, link or choice by ref. Returns the new screen. The result starts with 'Change: none | content changed | new screen | scrolled'. Work that starts on a tap (paying, saving, loading) can finish after this returns, so the screen may show 'Paying...' or a spinner. Do not report that as the result: pass wait_for with the text you expect (and gone: true for the spinner), or settle: true, before you read the outcome or do anything else.

ref.description: Element ref from the screen, e.g. e42

compact.description: When the change is 'content changed', return only the added/removed lines, not the whole screen

wait_for.description: Use after any action that starts work. Wait until this appears (a ref, a text, or role+name), or disappears with gone: true. The result says Waited: matched or timed out.

timeout_ms.description: How long wait_for and settle may take, in ms (default 2000)

settle.description: Wait until the screen stops changing (two equal reads 100 ms apart), up to timeout_ms. Use after any action that starts work. A slow result can still follow a pause, so prefer wait_for when you know the expected text.

tools.name: toggle_tile
tools.description: Flip a quick-settings tile in the open shade or Control Center. It changes the simulated device like set_device: Wi-Fi and mobile data both off take the network offline, dark_mode changes the app's colour scheme, dnd stops banners. Tiles: wifi, mobile_data, airplane, location, dark_mode, dnd, auto_rotate, flashlight (Android); airplane, wifi, mobile_data, focus, orientation_lock, brightness, dark_mode (iPhone). Fails with tile_not_visible if the panel is closed.

value.description: true or false; 0 to 100 for brightness. Omit to flip.

tools.name: type
tools.description: Type into a text field by ref (replaces its content). Returns the new screen. The result starts with 'Change: none | content changed | new screen | scrolled'. Also gives the field's value after typing.

ref.description: Element ref from the screen, e.g. e42

compact.description: When the change is 'content changed', return only the added/removed lines, not the whole screen

wait_for.description: Use after any action that starts work. Wait until this appears (a ref, a text, or role+name), or disappears with gone: true. The result says Waited: matched or timed out.

timeout_ms.description: How long wait_for and settle may take, in ms (default 2000)

settle.description: Wait until the screen stops changing (two equal reads 100 ms apart), up to timeout_ms. Use after any action that starts work. A slow result can still follow a pause, so prefer wait_for when you know the expected text.

tools.name: uninstall_app
tools.description: Remove an installed app from the phone. If it was open, the phone returns to the home screen. Fails with not_installed. Logged in device_log as simulated.

tools.name: unlock
tools.description: Swipe up on the lock screen. Returns to the same screen as before the lock. Fails with not_locked if the phone is not locked. Logged in device_log as simulated.

instructions:
You can use Shipvo apps the way a person uses them on a phone, without a phone.
Call open_app to get a session and the first screen. The screen is an accessibility tree: every button, field and text, with a [ref=eN]. Act with tap/type/scroll/back using refs, and read the screen that comes back each time.
Only what is on screen is listed, like a phone: a horizontal product rail shows a few items, so "scroll right" on the rail (its ref) to see more; "scroll down" the page for the rest.
System sheets (permission dialogs, the camera, the fingerprint prompt, payment prompts, notification banners, the share sheet) appear in the tree like any other screen: answer them by tapping, as a person would. Use set_device to decide what the phone has (a barcode in front of the camera, a location, whether the fingerprint matches, whether the payment is approved, network off) before the app asks for it.
Finish a task by checking the final screen says what you expected (for example "Order placed"). Call end_session when done to get a report.
